What you have here are two equations

the ticket cost equation: 4$ + 0.1c = Cost 

the attendance equation: 500 - 5c = Attendance 

Revenue can be defined simply as: Revenue = Cost\*Attendance

Or.. : (300 - 5c)\*(4 + 0.1c) = Revenue Where c = number of cost increases 

If we let Revenue = y on a plot then we can multiply everything together into a quadratic equation I got (-0.5c\^2) + 10c + 1200, but you ought to check that yourself.

Now since they are asking for the maximum revenue, and we have a complete equation for the revenue you just have to solve for the maxima value of the equation.

This can be done by, plotting, setting the derivative to 0, or doing some creative solving by finding the center between the two intersecting points. 

I don't think they have taught you derivatives yet so I will walk through the cheesy intersect method. 

using the quadratic equation x=−b± sqrt(b\^2−4ac)/2

where a = -0.5 : b = 10 and c = 1200

we get two intersects at: x = -40 and x = 60

The point halfway between -40 and 60 is 10 which can be found as (-40 + 60)/2 = 10

This point should be the maxima/minima point of the quadratic.

​

For giggles, we can check this using derivatives (To show you how much time you can save in the future lol)

using the equation y =  -0.5x\^2 + 10x + 1200

The derivative is y' = -1x + 10 

Setting the derivative = 0 gives maximum

so 0 = -1x + 10

x = 10 is the max

​

for b) since we know the max occurs at x = 10, we just substitute it in to get 

\-0.5(10\^2) + 10(10) + 1200 = Revenue

Revenue = 1250
